question: why did this book have such large drawdowns? walk me through what actually happened
answer:
The book had two drawdowns at least this deep in the last year, and the deepest one ran from 12.0% below the prior peak on 12.0%12.0%. I’m being careful not to overstate the path: drawdown depth is a peak-to-trough measure, not a simple return sum.
Deep drawdown episodes
2026-01-07 | 2026-03-27 | 12.0% | yes
2026-05-29 | 2026-06-25 | 6.24% | yes
In the first episode, the portfolio lost -12.0% over -12.0% sessions from the day after the peak to the trough, versus -7.80% for SPY over the same window. The broad selling was concentrated in the large growth holdings: MSFT fell the most in the window, while AMZN, GOOGL, LLY, JPM, NVDA and AAPL were also down; XOM was the main offset.
First drawdown, holding returns
MSFT | -26.0%
AMZN | -17.5%
GOOGL | -14.7%
LLY | -20.6%
JPM | -13.5%
NVDA | -11.4%
AAPL | -4.34%
XOM | 45.3%
In the second episode, the book lost -6.24% over -6.24% sessions from the late-May peak to the June trough, again worse than SPY at -2.68%. This one was led by MSFT, AMZN and AAPL, with GOOGL and NVDA also weak. JPM and the bond holdings helped, but not enough to stop the slide.
Second drawdown, holding returns
MSFT | -21.6%
AMZN | -16.1%
AAPL | -11.8%
GOOGL | -9.58%
NVDA | -7.19%
JPM | 12.0%
TLT | 2.25%
HYG | -0.03%
So the pattern is not one isolated event. The book was heavily concentrated in a handful of large-cap growth names, and when that cluster sold off together, the portfolio fell with it; when those names stabilised, the book recovered. The strongest diversifier in the first episode was XOM, and in the second episode JPM and the fixed-income holdings cushioned part of the move, but the concentration in MSFT, AAPL, AMZN, GOOGL and LLY left the book vulnerable to synchronized weakness.
